cases.purpose: blkid with no operand enumerates every probeable block device, including loop devices holding ext2, vfat, a DOS table with two ext2 partitions and a GPT with two ext2 partitions, with the same lines in the same order as util-linux blkid.
cases.oracle: util-linux blkid probing the same loop devices (images built identically by e2fsprogs mke2fs, dosfstools mkfs.vfat and sfdisk); loop device names are normalised to fixed labels.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and file tree.
cases.script:
. ./rl.sh
/usr/bin/truncate -s 2M a.img b.img c.img d.img
$MK -q -t ext2 -L ALPHA -U 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 a.img
/usr/sbin/mkfs.vfat -n BRAVO -i 1234ABCD b.img >/dev/null
/usr/sbin/sfdisk -q c.img <<'E'
label: dos
label-id: 0xc0ffee01
start=64, size=1024, type=83
start=1280, size=1024, type=83
E
/usr/sbin/sfdisk -q d.img <<'E'
label: gpt
label-id: 44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444
start=64, size=1024, type=L, uuid=55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555551, name="DELTAONE"
start=1280, size=1024, type=L, uuid=55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555552, name="DELTATWO"
E
at a.img; A=$REPLY; at b.img; B=$REPLY; at c.img; C=$REPLY; at d.img; D=$REPLY
$MK -q -t ext2 -L CHARLIE1 -U 66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666661 ${C}p1
$MK -q -t ext2 -L CHARLIE2 -U 66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666662 ${C}p2
$MK -q -t ext2 -L DELTAFS1 -U 77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777771 ${D}p1
$MK -q -t ext2 -L DELTAFS2 -U 77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777772 ${D}p2
reg ${C}p1 LOOP-C-p1; reg ${C}p2 LOOP-C-p2; reg ${D}p1 LOOP-D-p1; reg ${D}p2 LOOP-D-p2
reg $A LOOP-A; reg $B LOOP-B; reg $C LOOP-C; reg $D LOOP-D
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >o.txt 2>e.txt; local rc=$?; printf '[%s] status=%s\n' "$l" $rc; norm o.txt; echo "[stderr]"; norm e.txt; }
r enumerate-all blkid
